findings.text: follow-on: the enrichment eligibility predicate was widened back to `(p.should_enrich = true OR p.scan_relevance >= $minimum)`, dropping the `p.should_enrich IS NULL` guard the immediately-preceding promoted run (40ed29859163ab92a6e064fc66626ac0b8d27291) had put in place (frontier.py:296, parallel.py:305, parallel.py:423, parallel.py:851, frontier.py:2857, enrichment.py:624). Consequence: a path structurally marked should_enrich=false -- the VCS-repo-accessible-elsewhere and shallow-container cases set at frontier.py:1208 and frontier.py:1231 -- whose scan_relevance is at or above the scan threshold is once again pending and claimable, re-opening the du/rg-timeout and redundant-enrichment states those structural overrides exist to prevent (the comment at frontier.py:1228 names '/home, /usr, /opt -- du and rg will timeout'). The `p.total_dirs <= 500` claim filter and the `NOT (p.path_purpose IN $excluded_purposes)` clause cover the data-container and skipped-purpose cases; they do not cover a shallow container with 51-500 subdirs nor a repo accessible elsewhere. This is a deliberate revert, not a novel regression: the loose form is the long-standing original (present at 3dfed1125, before the section-63 series) and the run documents the intent in tests/discovery/test_path_enrich_failures.py::test_relevance_auto_enrich_keeps_triage_decision_through_budget, which asserts a should_enrich=false path is claimable. But section 63 asks only that a failing enrichment end; it does not ask to re-admit structurally-excluded paths, so this is a semantic change relative to the promoted predecessor that the coordinator should confirm rather than an error visible on a code-change basis.
findings.verification: Predicate traced across revisions with `git show <rev>:imas_codex/discovery/paths/frontier.py | grep 'should_enrich = true OR'`: 3dfed1125 and 3fb07d05e carry the loose form, 40ed29859163ab92a6e064fc66626ac0b8d27291 carries the IS NULL guard, 4c7e27d0 reverts to the loose form. Structural overrides read at frontier.py:1194-1243.

findings.text: follow-on: at the failure limit the path's reason is written to `p.enrich_error` while `p.enrich_skip_reason` is left untouched (parallel.py:1072-1074). enrich_skip_reason is the field documented 'Why not to enrich (if should_enrich=false)' (imas_codex/discovery/paths/models.py:121), so a reader inspecting that field cannot tell a path set aside by the budget from one never triaged; only the `enrich_failures` counter distinguishes it. The reason is not lost -- it is recorded in enrich_error and the run's test asserts it (test_reachable_failure_sets_path_aside_with_reason: `graph.reason == 'script failed'`). Recorded as a wording/observability follow-on, not a behavior defect.
findings.verification: Read at head: parallel.py:1063-1103. The removed base code set should_enrich=false and enrich_skip_reason=item.error at the limit; head keeps should_enrich and enrich_skip_reason untouched and relies on the counter predicate.

findings.text: follow-on: a budget-set-aside path (should_enrich true, scan_relevance >= minimum, enrich_failures >= ENRICH_FAILURE_LIMIT) is neither pending nor terminal. _count_terminal_paths (parallel.py:193-197) counts a path terminal only when `p.should_enrich = false AND p.scan_relevance < $minimum` or it is purpose-excluded or is_enriched, so the set-aside path (should_enrich true, relevance high) is not counted terminal, while every pending/claim query excludes it once the counter is exhausted. Under --path-limit accounting that path therefore neither advances the terminal count nor appears as pending. Pre-existing since the loose predicate (present at 3dfed1125); noted because this run makes the counter, not should_enrich, the set-aside signal and so makes the gap explicit.
findings.verification: Read parallel.py:180-206 at head; the terminal predicate requires `p.should_enrich = false AND p.scan_relevance < $minimum`, which a set-aside path fails on both the boolean and, by construction, the relevance term is >= minimum.

item_verdicts.goal: section 63 asks that path enrichment bound its failures like the code scan, set an exhausted path aside with its reason so the pending count drops, and (already delivered by the two predecessor runs) give the unreachability classifier and backoff one shared owner. This run keeps the budget and moves the exclusion off should_enrich onto a per-path `enrich_failures` counter declared in the facility schema, so a triage decision is no longer overwritten when a path exhausts its budget. It also closes the defect the previous review of this section recorded (the code-scan retry backoff firing only under a progress callback, now fixed and covered by test_reachable_failure_waits_with_or_without_progress_callback) and the associated private-helper follow-on (sleep_unless_stopped now public).

justifications.durability: the three done-when behaviours are guarded by tests that redden at base and green at head: baseline-scoped.log shows 4 failed / 3 passed at base for the two added regression tests plus one code-scan test, and committed-head.log shows 14 passed at head (reproduced by me). The counter exclusion is asserted against five independent surfaces (parallel.has_pending_work, parallel._has_pending_enrich_work, parallel.claim_paths_for_enriching, frontier.get_discovery_stats, enrichment.get_paths_pending_enrichment and frontier.claim_paths_for_enriching), and the code-scan backoff is asserted with and without a progress callback. The deduction is the test vehicle: PathGraph (tests/discovery/test_path_enrich_failures.py:105-176) mocks GraphClient with string-matching on the Cypher text rather than executing it, so a renamed property or a malformed statement would pass the unit tests; Cypher correctness rests on the separate read-only EXPLAIN arm (cypher-explain.log: 7/7 with a `Facility count=4` positive control), not on the tests.
justifications.evidence: the head arm is committed-head.log (14 passed / EXIT=0 at 4c7e27d0), reproduced by me as reviewer-head-gate.log. The negative control is genuine: negative-control.log runs negative-control.log's declared mutation (narrowing the enrich predicate to exclude should_enrich=false) and shows test_relevance_auto_enrich_keeps_triage_decision_through_budget failing with claim_paths_for_enriching returning [] instead of the path, EXIT=1, one failing id the head arm does not fail. The run also records a read-only EXPLAIN arm (7/7, positive control Facility count=4) and a build-models arm that generated FacilityPath.enrich_failures (build-models.log:12635). Against that, the manifest's structured baseline_suite is empty so the machine-readable base arm is absent, and the enrichment unit tests do not execute Cypher.
justifications.fit: the change follows the plan's idiom and the code-scan precedent it cites at section 63: a per-path counter that increments on a reachable failure, an exhausted path excluded from every frontier, and one shared owner for the classifier and backoff (already delivered by the predecessor). Mechanism-named symbols (enrich_failures, ENRICH_FAILURE_LIMIT, sleep_unless_stopped). The one deduction is the eligibility-predicate revert, which the plan does not call for and which re-admits structurally-excluded paths.
justifications.goal_fidelity: section 63's delivered behaviours all hold: an unreachable host pauses without charging, a reachable failure is set aside after the limit with its reason, and the pending count then excludes it. This run additionally stops the budget from overwriting the triage should_enrich decision and repairs the code-scan retry-wait regression the previous review of this section recorded, so the section's composite goal is fully met. The residual is that the counter mechanism is implemented by widening the eligibility predicate rather than by keeping the guard, which changes which paths are enriched in a way section 63 does not ask for.
justifications.reuse: the run retires a duplicated writer (frontier.mark_enrichment_complete now delegates to parallel.mark_enrichment_complete) and promotes the shared sleep helper from a private cross-module name to a public import held by base/reachability.py and reached by code/workers.py -- the single-owner outcome the section asked for -- without copying either.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff against 40ed29859163ab92a6e064fc66626ac0b8d27291 is the eight declared code/test paths and nothing else; no shared index, sprint state, plan file or generated artifact was staged.
